newsitem.title: USA: NYC gets $134 mln of retail bond orders on 1st day.
newsitem.headline: NYC gets $134 mln of retail bond orders on 1st day.

text.p: New York City, which is selling $900 million of tax-exempt bonds on April 9, said on Friday that individual investors ordered $134 million of its bonds during the first day of the presale period.
"That's a good, solid day," said a city official, who declined to be named.

The city in the past has gotten $150 million to $200 million of retail orders for its bonds and the city official noted that the first day of the presale period did not start until noon on Friday, suggesting retail investors stepped up to the plate fairly quickly.
The retail presale period ends on April 8 at noon, one day before the bond offering will be priced for institutional investors.

New York City sold out the first two maturities, 1999 and 2000, and while the next three maturities also proved especially popular with individual investors, they also were interested in longer maturities, the official said.

"We're very hopeful about perhaps selling out 2001, 2002 and 2003, but not yet," he added. New York City also is selling about $122 million of taxable bonds as part of the same bond sale, and around $50 million of this debt was earmarked for European investors.
